name: Museum of West African Art (MOWAA)
funding: Founding partners: Edo State Government, Germany's Foreign Office, Mellon Foundation, British Museum, PI Trust. Leadership Circle donors include NNPC Seplat Energy, Lekoil Nigeria and Azura Power West Africa.
watch: Oba loyalists disrupted the 9 November 2025 preview. Edo's Assembly urged a state takeover on 22 December 2025.
why_flagged: Founding partners: Edo State Government, Germany's Foreign Office, Mellon Foundation, British Museum, PI Trust. Leadership Circle donors include NNPC Seplat Energy, Lekoil Nigeria and Azura Power West Africa.
records_note: It names donors by tier (undated) and eight trustees, but posts no annual report or accounts.

name: Mystetskyi Arsenal
funding: State enterprise. 2025: UAH 38.0M state budget, UAH 24.2M own income. Project partners include Erste Foundation, British Council, the US Embassy and International Renaissance Foundation.
watch: In July 2013 the director had Volodymyr Kuznetsov's painting painted black and Vasyl Tsagolov's work excluded; artists called a boycott. 2025 visitors: 53,870.
why_flagged: State enterprise. 2025: UAH 38.0M state budget, UAH 24.2M own income. Project partners include Erste Foundation, British Council, the US Embassy and International Renaissance Foundation.
records_note: It posts annual reports for 2017 to 2025 and audited statements for 2014 to 2019; the 2025 report names partners; no board is listed.

name: National Art Museum of Ukraine
funding: State museum. The Cabinet gave it UAH 5.6M in 2020 for emergency facade repairs. Donations go to its own charitable foundation.
watch: In October 2012 staff sent an open letter demanding the removal of acting director Tatiana Mironova; art workers backed it with a statement and petition.
why_flagged: State museum. The Cabinet gave it UAH 5.6M in 2020 for emergency facade repairs. Donations go to its own charitable foundation. No corporate sponsor list is published.
records_note: Its public information page holds a 2021 budget and utility compliance notes only; no annual report, accounts, donor list or board.

name: Museo de la Solidaridad Salvador Allende
funding: Servicio Nacional del Patrimonio Cultural grant of CLP 660M in 2025. Project money from Fondart, the Senate, Henry Moore Foundation and Centro Cultural de España. Metro is a media partner.
watch: In 2023 Allende's grandson wrote to the museum, then campaigned publicly, demanding Tania Bruguera's show be cancelled. It opened late and modified.
why_flagged: Servicio Nacional del Patrimonio Cultural grant of CLP 660M in 2025. Project money from Fondart, the Senate, Henry Moore Foundation and Centro Cultural de España. Metro is a media partner.
records_note: It posts annual reports for 2014 to 2025, balances, a 2025 list of funders and agreements, and five named directors.

name: Museo de Arte de Puerto Rico
funding: Private nonprofit. Current exhibitions are backed by the Flamboyan Foundation, Mellon Foundation, Helen Frankenthaler Foundation, Mano Amiga and the Puerto Rico Tourism Company.
watch: On 19 November 2023 activists picketed after the Cecilia Orta Allende gallery was renamed for a donor family tied to the Fiscal Oversight Board.
why_flagged: Private nonprofit. Current exhibitions are backed by the Flamboyan Foundation, Mellon Foundation, Helen Frankenthaler Foundation, Mano Amiga and the Puerto Rico Tourism Company. No corporate donors are named.
records_note: Its site names 19 board members but posts no annual report, accounts or donor list; Form 990s for 2000 to 2025 are on ProPublica.

name: Nairobi National Museum
funding: National Museums of Kenya, a state corporation, runs it. Planet Africa (2024 to 2025) was funded by the German Research Foundation and Germany's Foreign Office.
watch: In May 2017 museum management pulled works by Michael Soi, Patrick Mukabi and Bertiers Mbatia on opening day, saying they were unsuitable for children.
why_flagged: Run by National Museums of Kenya, a state corporation. The Planet Africa project (opened November 2024) lists the German Research Foundation and Germany's Foreign Office as funders. No sponsor list.
records_note: No records of its own: parent National Museums of Kenya posts annual reports for 2015 to 2019 and names its board; no accounts or donors.

name: National Museum of Fine Arts of Chile (MNBA)
funding: State museum under the Servicio Nacional del Patrimonio Cultural; buys works from its own budget. Gifts came through Fundación AMA from collector Juan Yarur Torres and from artist Cecilia Vicuña.
watch: 510,720 visitors in 2024, a decade high. Cancelled a León Ferrari retrospective in June 2026, citing budget cuts. Not the Buenos Aires museum.
records_note: MNBA has no records of its own; its parent service posts accountability reports 2006 to 2026 and financial statements 2017 to 2025.

name: Bienal de Cuenca
funding: Run by the Fundación Municipal Bienal de Cuenca, a city body. The 17th edition cost about $1.2M, from municipal money, private-company agreements and self-raised funds.
watch: In November 2025 a private group, DPOT, threatened the biennial over one work. It filed a complaint and kept the work on view.
records_note: Posts one annual report, for 2023, naming its agreement partners and the $163,913 raised; no accounts, board or standing sponsor page found.

name: Fábrica de Arte Cubano
funding: Founded by musician X Alfonso. In 2014 the Cuban Music Institute and Ministry of Culture were covering some costs until it became self-financing.
watch: The ministry's music centre cancelled a Celia Cruz tribute there in October 2025. It closed temporarily in June 2026; Prensa Latina blames the US embargo.
why_flagged: Founded by musician X Alfonso. In 2014 the Cuban Music Institute and Ministry of Culture covered some costs until it became self-financing. It occupies a state-owned building.
records_note: Its site offers two dossiers and nothing else: no annual report, accounts, sponsor list or board.

name: Biennale Jogja
funding: Organised by Yayasan Biennale Yogyakarta, a state-funded foundation created in 2010. The Yogyakarta regional government ran the 2019 edition.
watch: On 9 October 2026 it announced closure after 16 years, citing rising censorship and violence against activists. It names no incident against itself.
records_note: Lists its patron board and executive but dated 2015; no annual reports, accounts or funder names are published.

name: Jakarta Biennale
funding: Run since 2024 by Majelis Jakarta, an artist-collective network. 2026 partners: Dulux, Artotel's Paviliun Raden Saleh, iForte. Jakarta culture office and Jakpro logos are unlabelled; no budget published.
watch: Founded 1974 by the Jakarta Arts Council. The 2026 edition, KEBAL, runs 4 Oct to 28 Nov at Taman Ismail Marzuki.
records_note: The partner page shows sponsor and media-partner logos with role labels only; no reports, accounts, dates or board are published.

name: Ayala Museum
funding: Run privately by Ayala Foundation, the Ayala group's foundation. Ayala Corporation co-presents shows; BPI is a partner. The Spanish and US embassies supported the 2024 Zóbel show.
watch: Opened 1967 from Fernando Zobel's plan. It closed in 2019 for rebuilding and reopened 4 December 2021. It had 65,000 visitors in 2014.
records_note: No records of its own; parent Ayala Foundation posts annual reports 2019 to 2024, 2024 financial statements and its trustees, with partner logos only.
